The government is implementing tiered fuel pricing schemes to manage consumption, but these measures have been met with resistance due to economic hardship and social concerns. President Masoud Pezeshkian has urged citizens to conserve energy, while officials acknowledge that reforming energy prices is not feasible in the current climate.

articles.title: RBI likely to hold rates as West Asia crisis impact on growth remains unclear: Bank of Baroda Report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to maintain interest rates on Friday, June 5th, as the impact of the ongoing West Asia crisis on economic growth remains unclear. The central bank will likely continue its data-dependent approach, balancing growth concerns with inflation risks and global uncertainties.  Bank of Baroda, a financial institution, anticipates an upward revision in RBI's CPI projection for FY27 due to rising fuel prices and expects the RBI to retain its neutral policy stance.

articles.title: ADB, StanChart ink partnership to support Indian firms across supply chains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Standard Chartered Bank have signed agreements to strengthen supply chain finance in India. The agreements, including a risk participation arrangement through Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) and a partial guarantee facility agreement, aim to expand access to trade and supply chain finance for businesses operating in India. These arrangements are intended to support the continued flow of cross-border and domestic trade, particularly by addressing financing gaps for emerging and underserved segments like distributor financing, which often involves small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This partnership aligns with ADB's strategic priority to promote inclusive economic growth and financial deepening across Asia and the Pacific.

articles.title: Fund crunch paralyses cultural academies in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's premier cultural academies are facing a severe financial crisis, leading to salary delays and administrative disruptions. The Kerala Sahitya Akademi and Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Akademi have been unable to pay salaries due to delayed government funding. The situation is further complicated by the absence of governing bodies following a change in government, hindering decision-making and financial transactions. Cultural organization Samskara Sahithi has called for an inquiry into alleged misuse of funds and demanded new governing bodies and a 'cultural White Paper'.

articles.title: Thrissur Corporation bags Paristhithi Mithram Award 2026 for green governance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Thrissur Municipal Corporation has been awarded the prestigious ‘Paristhithi Mithram Award 2026’ for its exemplary environmental protection efforts. The award, recognizing the corporation's achievements in waste management, water conservation, and greening initiatives, will be presented at the State-level World Environment Day celebrations in Thiruvananthapuram. The Kerala State Biodiversity Board, the Directorate of Environment and Climate Change, and the Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment jointly organized the event.

articles.title: What keeps the Grand Canyon alive: Scientists reveal a hidden underground system beneath one of Earth’s greatest wonders | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Northern Arizona University scientists are studying the Grand Canyon's hidden underground water system, which supports wildlife and visitors.  Researchers use lidar technology to map cave passages and analyze patterns in rock formations that influence water flow. The team is also examining decades of snow and climate data to understand how changes in snowfall affect groundwater systems. This research aims to better understand how water moves through the canyon's subsurface and what threats it faces due to drought conditions.

articles.title: Assam, Meghalaya farmers resume farming in disputed border area after weeks of conflict - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Villagers in Assam and Meghalaya resumed farming activities in a disputed border area after weeks of intermittent conflict. The resumption followed an agreement brokered by representatives from the two state governments, who met on Tuesday to resolve the dispute in the Tapat-Lapangap sector. Deimonmi Lyngdoh, head of Lapangap's traditional community organization, expressed hope that this temporary arrangement would strengthen relations and contribute towards a lasting resolution of border issues.  This agreement is part of a larger effort to resolve 12 disputed sectors along their 855-kilometer border since 1972.

articles.title: Henry Nowak murder protest turns violent: 11 police officers injured, 2 arrested after Sikh man jailed for life - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Violent clashes erupted in Southampton after the sentencing of Vickrum Digwa, who was convicted of murdering 18-year-old student Henry Nowak.  Protests, fueled by public anger over police handling of the case, escalated into disorder with protesters throwing objects at riot police and damaging property. Two individuals have been arrested for their involvement in the disturbances, while Sarah Jones confirmed that police will review footage from various sources as investigations continue. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood condemned the violence, emphasizing that attacks on officers and public disorder are unacceptable.

articles.title: Thiruvananthapuram airport inducts Kerala’s first HRET crash fire tender - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport has acquired a state-of-the-art Rosenbauer Panther Crash Fire Tender equipped with a High Reach Extendable Turret (HRET). This is the first of its kind at any airport in Kerala, and it significantly enhances firefighting capabilities. The HRET can reach heights of 16.5 meters, pierce aircraft fuselages, and deliver extinguishing agents directly into passenger cabins or cargo holds, improving fire suppression and passenger survivability.  The vehicle also features a thermal imaging camera for accurate fire detection and control, as well as advanced pump and roll functionality for rapid response.

articles.title: Ukraine Drone Strikes: Ukraine drones strike St Petersburg oil terminal, naval base as Russia reports bus attack killing 8 civilians - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine launched drone strikes targeting energy and military facilities in St Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, disrupting operations at the main airport and communications ahead of the annual St Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF).  The attacks came hours after a deadly wave of Russian missile and drone strikes on Ukrainian cities. Zelenskyy claimed the drones flew over 1,000 kilometers to hit the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and targeted the Kronstadt naval base, home to Russia's Baltic Fleet. Russia responded with threats of systemic retaliation, accusing Ukraine of a "terrorist attack" on a passenger bus in the Russian-controlled part of the Donetsk region, which killed eight civilians. The escalating drone war reflects the intensifying tit-for-tat campaign between the two countries.

articles.title: How the D-day unfolded for DKS, reaching across political divide - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D.K. Shivakumar, the newly sworn-in Chief Minister of Karnataka, began his day with personal and political gestures, including calls to MLAs and a visit to former Chief Ministers B.S. Yediyurappa and H.D. Deve Gowda. He chose traditional attire for his oath ceremony and invited Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Sonia Gandhi to the event, which was attended by high-ranking members of the Congress party from other states.  The ceremony also included a gathering of religious leaders representing various faiths.

articles.title: They introduced a fly to save Fiji's coconuts—then an entire species vanished | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The introduction of the parasitic fly, Bessa remota, to Fiji as a biological pest control measure for coconut plantations resulted in the extinction of the native Fijian Coconut Moth, Levuana iridescens.  This case study highlights the potential ecological risks associated with invasive species and biological control programs. While intended to protect crops, the introduction led to the loss of a unique species and serves as a cautionary tale for modern conservation efforts.

articles.title: AITUC holds solidarity rally for Cuba in Thrissur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: WFTU deputy general secretary C. Sreekumar and other trade union leaders from the AITUC organized a solidarity rally in Thrissur, Kerala, to support the Cuban people.  The event saw strong participation from workers and trade union leaders who condemned U.S. sanctions on Cuba and expressed solidarity with the Cuban people.

articles.title: 121-million-year-old bird fossil stuns scientists with tail feathers twice the length of its body | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A museum in China has revealed a fossil of an ancient bird, Plumadraco bankoorum, that lived 121 million years ago. The discovery of the bird's tail feathers, which extend far beyond typical proportions for its size, has sparked interest among researchers.  The fossil, part of a larger collection of ancient bird remains, was examined after being stored for years and revealed details about the bird's plumage structure, including pigmentation and feather arrangement.

articles.title: The dark side of plastic recycling: Why some waste ends up being burned | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Developed countries have been exporting plastic waste to poorer nations for processing, but a significant portion is not properly recycled due to contamination. This leads to open burning of plastic, which releases harmful pollutants into the atmosphere and poses health risks to both local communities and ecosystems. Dr Therese M. Karlsson of the International Pollutants Elimination Network (IPEN) highlights that open burning is a prevalent form of plastic pollution globally, while Joseph Hoover, from the Indigenous Resilience Centre, emphasizes the detrimental impact on air quality and public health. Addressing this issue requires improved recycling infrastructure, reduced plastic production, better waste management practices, and increased transparency in international plastic trade.

articles.title: “Telangana is the Jagir of its four crore people”, KTR tells Pawan Kalyan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.T. Rama Rao, working president of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), criticized Pawan Kalyan, Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister, for his comments about Telangana being "no one's jagir."  Rama Rao asserted that Telangana was indeed the "jagir of four crore Telangana people" and accused Pawan Kalyan of undermining the sacrifices made for statehood. He also questioned why only the Telangana movement is portrayed negatively while similar movements elsewhere are celebrated.

articles.title: Gujarat launches massive anti-infiltration drive; 362 detained in Operation Delta Hunt - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Gujarat Police conducted a statewide crackdown, "Operation Delta Hunt," detaining 362 undocumented Bangladeshi immigrants and questioning over 782 suspected foreign nationals. The operation, launched on June 2nd and continuing into early Wednesday, targeted cities like Ahmedabad, Surat, Rajkot, Vadodara, and others.  Deputy Chief Minister and Home Minister Harsh Sanghavi stated that the operation reflects a "zero tolerance" policy towards illegal immigration and national security threats. Mr. Sanghavi also emphasized that authorities are investigating local agents and facilitators involved in providing accommodation, jobs, and forged documents to facilitate illegal stay. The operation is ongoing with further raids expected in the coming days.

articles.title: Donald Trump Netanyahu Phone Call: ‘I was a little bit perturbed’: Donald Trump confirms calling Netanyahu 'crazy' over Lebanon strikes, defends working relationship - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump confirmed using expletive-laden language during a phone call with Benjamin Netanyahu, calling the Israeli Prime Minister "f***ing crazy" due to his military escalation in Lebanon.  Trump, however, insisted that their working relationship remained strong and he expected a resolution to regional tensions quickly. The president also linked the conflict to broader geopolitical negotiations involving Iran, suggesting that escalating violence risks undermining discussions on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Despite concerns about civilian casualties and regional spillovers, Trump expressed optimism for a diplomatic solution in Lebanon.

articles.title: A Crash Course in Mountain Bike Suspension (2026) | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Vernon Felton, director of product at Canyon, and former editor at Pinkbike and Bike magazine, explains how mountain bike suspension works.  Suspension, which typically uses a spring or air spring to absorb impact from rocks and roots, is designed to make riding over rough terrain easier and more comfortable. Different types of mountain biking require different amounts of suspension travel, with cross-country bikes having less travel than trail, enduro, and downhill bikes. Ebike suspension differs because it adds a motor and battery, which impacts the performance of the suspension.  To find the best ebike suspension, consumers should prioritize quality over weight reduction, opting for brands like RockShox, Fox, Cane Creek, and Marzocchi.

articles.title: UPSC Essentials subject-wise quiz : Science and Technology (Week 165)
articles.rephrased_article:
UPSC Essentials brings a subject-wise quiz on Science and Technology. The quizzes are designed to help revise important topics from the static part of the syllabus. The Indian Express published the UPSC essentials magazine for May 2026, which includes questions related to stealth technology, space technology, black boxes, defense hardware, and Dual Frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar (DFSAR).  

These questions cover current affairs-linked topics in Science and Technology, including advancements in aircraft design, military modernization, space exploration, and the use of radar technology.

articles.title: Nvidia’s RTX Spark Laptops Look Hell-Bent on Disruption | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Nvidia has announced the RTX Spark, a new line of laptops designed to bring AI processing power to local Windows PCs. The chips combine unified memory, RTX graphics, and an N1 CPU, offering performance comparable to the MacBook Pro. Microsoft, meanwhile, is releasing its own Surface Laptop Ultra, which aims to compete with the Mac Pro as a high-performance device for AI enthusiasts. These new products could significantly impact the PC market, potentially challenging existing players like Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm.

articles.title: Honey-Trap Accused Found HIV+ Sparks Major Health Scare In Madhya Pradesh
articles.rephrased_article: A woman arrested in Madhya Pradesh for her involvement in a honey-trap racket has been found to be HIV-positive.  The case, which began with a farmer's allegations of blackmail, has now raised concerns about potential exposure to the virus among several men who may have interacted with the accused. Police are investigating and working to identify those involved, while health experts will provide confidential testing and counseling for identified individuals. The development highlights the significant public health concern surrounding HIV in India, where over 25 lakh people live with the virus.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Potential mass exposure to HIV due to criminal activity raises serious public health concerns.

articles.title: 10 must-read Julia Quinn Regency romances for Bridgerton fans | Books and Literature News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Julia Quinn, author of the Bridgerton series, has written several other swoon-worthy historical Regency romances. These novels feature strong female characters and captivating love stories set in the 19th century.  Quinn's works include "The Duke and I," a tale of a charming highwayman who falls for a companion to the dowager duchess; "An Earl's Redemption," where an American heiress encounters the Duke of Ashbourne; and "A Most Unexpected Bride," which follows a governess and an earl as they navigate their feelings.

articles.title: US-Iran Live Updates: Trump Says 'Would Like To Meet' Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei
articles.rephrased_article: Iran carried out a drone attack on Kuwait International Airport, wounding several people and forcing air traffic to be suspended. The US responded with strikes on Iranian targets in response to attacks across the Middle East.  Kuwait intercepted missile and drone attacks, while Bahrain also reported attacks. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated that all Iranian missiles failed to hit their targets.

articles.title: North Korea Women's Footballers Break Down in Tears Meeting Kim Jong Un After Historic South Korea Visit and $1 Million Title Win
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Express Global Desk provides authoritative coverage of international developments, focusing on US and Canadian immigration policies. The desk's team of experienced journalists, led by Aniruddha Dhar, Nischai Vats, and Mashkoora Khan, delivers verified information through breaking news, in-depth analysis, and policy updates.  Their reporting adheres to strict editorial standards and relies on official data for accuracy and clarity.

articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar Takes Oath, G Parameshwara Is His Deputy
articles.rephrased_article: DK Shivakumar, a prominent figure in the Congress, took oath as the Chief Minister of Karnataka, ending a two-year political tussle. His cabinet of 13 ministers includes his predecessor's son, Yathindra Siddaramaiah.  G Parameshwara was appointed Deputy Chief Minister, balancing social factions within the party. The event saw participation from Congress leaders like Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and other state chief ministers. Shivakumar expressed gratitude to the Gandhi family for their support in his political journey.

articles.title: Make Satish Jarkiholi KPCC president, say AHINDA district units - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AHINDA leaders and various organizations in Karnataka have demanded that Minister Satish Jarkiholi be appointed as the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president. They argue that this would strengthen the AHINDA movement and ensure support from all deprived communities.  The demands come after Jarkiholi's successful track record in organizing the AHINDA movement and his popularity among various communities, including Muslims.

articles.title: How to Block Spam Calls and Spam Texts on iPhone and Android (2026) | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: WIRED offers guidance on blocking unwanted calls and messages.  The article explains that while avoiding answering unknown numbers is helpful, it's not always feasible for all situations. It also recommends using the "Do Not Call Registry" to prevent sales calls from reputable companies but notes its limited effectiveness. WIRED provides instructions on how to block individual numbers, filter unknown callers and senders on both iPhone and Android devices.  Major carriers like AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, Google Fi, and US Cellular offer apps that can help identify and block nuisance calls or messages. The article cautions users about third-party apps and advises caution when using them due to privacy concerns.

articles.title: 'It's not nice': Donald Trump says US has 'other way' to deal with Iran - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated he must decide between negotiating a deal with Iran or pursuing an alternative, which he described as "not nice." He expressed preference for a diplomatic approach but acknowledged the possibility of military action. The US leader emphasized that bombing could achieve similar results without deploying ground troops. This comes amid escalating tensions in the Middle East following recent attacks on US allies by Iran, who retaliated against US-Israeli strikes in late February.

articles.title: Deserted streets, people glued to TV: D K Shivakumar’s Dodda Alahalli during his swearing-in | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: D K Shivakumar, the newly sworn-in chief minister of Karnataka, took his oath in Bengaluru while his home village, Dodda Alahalli, observed the event with a mix of excitement and pride.  Many villagers traveled to the capital city for the occasion, while others remained in their homes. Shivakumar's childhood friend, Nagaraj, recalled playing marbles with him as children, highlighting his humble beginnings and enduring bond with his hometown.  The village also boasts numerous amenities, including a solar plant and government facilities, reflecting its development under Shivakumar's leadership.

articles.title: Indian Killed In Iranian Attack On Kuwait Airport
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian national was killed and at least 63 others were injured in an attack on Kuwait International Airport.  The Iranian Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility for the attack, stating it was a retaliation for US attacks on an Iranian oil tanker and island. Kuwait's health ministry reported injuries including head wounds, cerebral hemorrhages, amputations, and blast injuries. The Indian Embassy in Kuwait expressed condolences to the bereaved family and is coordinating with Kuwaiti authorities.  The attack caused damage to airport facilities and led to the suspension of air traffic at the airport.

articles.title: Dhurandhar to release in Japan after earning Rs 3100 cr, can it break Dangal’s record? | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Jyoti Deshpande, President, Media & Content Business at Jio Studios and Reliance Industries, believes that Indian cinema is making progress in non-English speaking international markets.  She cites the success of "Dhurandhar" as an example, noting its strong performance in Germany and upcoming releases in Japan. While acknowledging the industry's focus on pan-India successes, Deshpande emphasizes the importance of creating stories that transcend language barriers and matching global production standards. She believes that regional films like "Raja Shivaji" are a step towards strengthening regional cinema and achieving broader appeal.  Deshpande argues that India's linguistic diversity remains a challenge but that success in international markets will depend on breaking down language barriers and producing high-quality content that resonates with global audiences.

articles.title: CarryMen: India start-up offering shopping bag carriers sparks debate on entitlement
articles.rephrased_article: A new start-up called CarryMen in Delhi offers shoppers assistance with carrying bags and navigating crowded markets. The service, launched in April, provides male and female assistants for up to four hours at a cost of 79 rupees ($0.83; £0.62) for 30 minutes or 149 rupees for an hour.  While some customers praise the service as helpful, others criticize it as indicative of entitlement and exploitative labor practices. The founders argue that the service is simply providing assistance to those who need help navigating crowded markets and are not exploiting workers. CarryMen plans to expand its services in other markets across India.

articles.title: DRC suggests behind-closed-doors World Cup warm-up to offset Ebola threat | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is considering playing their pre-World Cup friendly against Chile behind closed doors after the mayor of La Linea de la Concepcion, Spain, banned the match due to health concerns regarding the Ebola outbreak in the country. Sebastien Desabre, head coach of the DRC, expressed hope for the match to still take place and said they are taking all necessary precautions, including following FIFA's medical organization guidelines. The DRC is currently based in Belgium after cancelling a planned training camp at home due to the Ebola outbreak.

articles.title: She watched a wildfire destroy her town, so she's building fire-proof bunkers
articles.rephrased_article: Linda Cantey, an aerospace engineer, was deeply affected by the 2017 Atlas wildfire that destroyed her California town.  She channeled her grief into action, collaborating with a mining company to develop the above-ground refuge bunker called Fort. The Fort is designed to withstand fire and hold up to eight people for four hours. Other solutions include high-tech hydraulic homes from Holden Forrest's HiberTec Homes and goat herds used for fire mitigation by companies like Kimberly Jones' Goat Mowers LLC and Tim Arrowsmith's Western Grazers. These innovative approaches aim to mitigate wildfire damage, but they are expensive and not a complete solution.

articles.title: Iran’s World Cup squad to depart for Mexico on June 6 despite US visa delay | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s World Cup squad will depart for their base camp in Mexico on June 6 despite ongoing uncertainty surrounding US visa issues.  The team, which has been training in Turkey since February, is scheduled to arrive in Mexico on Sunday. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the delegation would not be allowed to include members with ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The team's departure comes after a previous incident in April when an Iranian delegation was denied entry to Canada due to alleged IRGC connections.

articles.title: The end of Trump’s 'weaponization' fund is another sign Republicans are fighting back
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Justice (DOJ) abandoned its "anti-weaponisation" fund after intense backlash from Republicans in Congress. The fund, intended to compensate individuals wrongly targeted by the Biden administration, was met with criticism for potentially shielding rioters involved in the January 6th attack on the US Capitol and providing tax benefits to Trump allies.  Senate Republicans joined Democrats in criticizing the fund, stalling immigration legislation as a result of the controversy. Despite the DOJ's decision to suspend the program, critics continue to challenge its legality and demand its permanent abolition. The issue is likely to remain contentious as it could impact future presidential actions and influence the 2024 election.

articles.title: New York police investigate videos of men emerging from city's sewer system
articles.rephrased_article: New York police are investigating videos showing groups of men entering the city's sewer system. The men, believed to be treasure hunters or urban explorers, were seen removing manhole covers and descending into the sewers before re-emerging hours later. The Department of Environmental Protection warned that entering the sewer system is illegal and dangerous due to potential hazards.  Police are still investigating and no arrests have been made.

articles.title: Indonesia: Prabowo fires head of free meals scheme plagued by mass poisonings
articles.rephrased_article: President Prabowo Subianto has fired the head of the free meals program, Dadan Hindayana, amid allegations of corruption and food poisoning. The program, designed to provide free meals to 80 million school children, has been plagued by health issues and financial concerns since its launch last year.  The sacking comes after a complaint from Indonesia's corruption watchdog and as the program was recently scaled back due to the war in Iran. Critics argue that the changes are cosmetic and do not address the program's systemic problems.

articles.title: Los Angeles mayoral race results
articles.rephrased_article: Karen Bass advanced to the November run-off election for Los Angeles mayor, with votes still being counted.  She faces a potential challenge from either fellow Democrat Nithya Raman or Republican newcomer Spencer Pratt. The winner will lead the second-largest city in the US and face issues like homelessness and affordable housing as Los Angeles prepares for the 2028 Olympics. California's governor's race is also still pending, with frontrunners including Steve Hilton, Xavier Becerra, and Tom Steyer.

articles.title: Trump May Have New Plans For How America Deals With China
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth, Secretary of War, articulated a new US defense strategy at the Shangri-La Dialogue.  He emphasized competition with China while acknowledging recent improvements in relations and emphasizing transactional partnerships with allies. The speech highlighted India's growing role as a regional security partner, signaling increased American reliance on its military capabilities and industrial base. Hegseth also called for greater burden-sharing from allies to enhance deterrence and sustain US influence in the Indo-Pacific region.  The strategy aims to achieve these objectives through tangible military preparedness, strategic partnerships, and a focus on reciprocity rather than open-ended commitments.

articles.title: ‘Doesn’t seem qualified’: Who is Bill Pulte, acting US intelligence chief? | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump appointed businessman and federal housing regulator Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence (DNI).  Pulte, a graduate of Northwestern University, has no experience in intelligence operations but is heir to his family's large homebuilding firm, PulteGroup. Pulte will oversee 18 intelligence departments including the CIA and NSA, but faces skepticism from lawmakers who question his qualifications for the role. Some senators have called him a "partisan thug" and expressed concerns that he lacks the necessary national security experience.  The Senate is expected to decide on his permanent appointment in the coming months.
